author: Rahul kp
topic: Valuation of Unsold Stock on Consignment
title: Consignment
hook: stock carries its share of cost!
simple_words: Unsold goods with the consignee are valued at their cost plus their share of the expenses spent to bring them to the godown.

definitions.meaning: Goods sent to the consignee but not sold by the end of the period. They still belong to the consignor and are shown in his books.
One-time costs up to the godown: freight, insurance, loading, octroi, unloading. They are added to the value of stock.
definitions.note: Godown rent and selling cost are not added

key_points: Value unsold stock at ==cost== (or loaded invoice value) plus its proportionate non-recurring expenses.
Add !!all non-recurring expenses up to the godown for the whole consignment!!, whoever paid them: consignor or consignee.
Recurring expenses (godown rent, salary, selling expenses) are never added to stock.
If goods were sent at invoice price above cost, take stock at invoice value plus expenses, then remove the loading through ==Stock Reserve==.
formula_hook: take the unsold share, U over Q

formulas.name: Value of unsold stock
formulas.legend: U = units unsold, Q = units sent, C = cost (or loaded invoice value) of goods sent, E = non-recurring expenses up to godown

entries.label: Closing stock at year end
entries.narration: Being unsold stock at cost (or loaded invoice value) plus proportionate expenses

entries.label: Goods sent at loaded price
entries.narration: Being loading on unsold stock removed by reserve

insight.text: First total all non-recurring expenses for the whole consignment, then take only the U/Q portion into stock.

memory_trick.mnemonic: Till the Door, Not the Floor
memory_trick.explanation: Expenses up to the godown door go into stock. Expenses after the door, on the godown floor (rent, selling), go to the Consignment A/c as expenses.

steps: Find Q, U and the unsold ratio U/Q
Add them to cost or invoice value
Pass stock entry; reserve if loaded
exam_tip: Check whether goods were sent at cost or invoice price. If at invoice price, create Stock Reserve on the loading in unsold stock.

doubt.question: Should consignee's unloading expenses go into stock?
doubt.answer: Yes, if they are non-recurring and incurred up to the godown. Octroi and unloading paid by the consignee are added, the same as the consignor's freight.

mistakes.wrong: Adding expenses only for the unsold units, or leaving out the consignee's unloading and octroi
mistakes.right: Add all non-recurring expenses up to the godown for the whole consignment, whoever paid them, then take unsold proportion U/Q.

mistakes.wrong: Adding godown rent or selling expenses to the value of closing stock
mistakes.right: Only non-recurring expenses up to the godown go into stock. Recurring expenses are charged to Consignment A/c.

mistakes.wrong: Valuing unsold stock at invoice price and stopping there
mistakes.right: Take loaded invoice value plus expenses, then create Stock Reserve for the loading on unsold goods.

mistakes.wrong: Showing consignment stock in the consignee's books
mistakes.right: Unsold stock belongs to the consignor and is valued in his books. The consignee only reports it as goods held.

Checker 1: Mistake 1 (wrong): the phrase "Adding expenses only for the unsold units" is ambiguous. The correct method itself adds only the unsold units' share of expenses (U/Q), so this part of the 'mistake' reads like the right method. Suggested rewording: "Adding only the expenses that seem to relate to unsold goods, or leaving out the consignee's unloading and octroi, instead of totalling all non-recurring expenses for the whole consignment and then taking the U/Q share."
